looks.name: Wallis Dress
looks.description: Wallis Simpson wore this wedding ensemble by the American designer Mainbocher when she married the Duke of Windsor, the former King Edward VIII, at the Chateau de Cande in France on June 3, 1937. Edward had abdicated in December 1936 so that he could marry her. Its silk was dyed a color created for her, Wallis blue, but the dye has since faded.

looks.name: Zoot Suit
looks.description: The zoot suit paired a thigh-length jacket with wide padded shoulders and broad lapels with high-waisted, full-legged trousers that narrowed to tight cuffs. It first caught on among young Black men in Harlem in the 1930s, then spread to Mexican American and Filipino American youth in the West. After 1942 wool limits, many white Americans saw it as unpatriotic, and it became the target of the 1943 Zoot Suit Riots in Los Angeles.

looks.name: New Look Dress
looks.description: Christian Dior showed his first collection in Paris in spring 1947 and introduced the silhouette known as the New Look. Its rounded shoulders, small cinched waist, emphasized hips and very full skirt broke with the uniforms, restrictions and shortages of the war years. Its success helped postwar Paris regain its standing as the capital of fashion.

looks.name: Mondrian Dress
looks.description: Yves Saint Laurent showed his Mondrian dresses in his fall/winter 1965-66 collection, after reading a book about the painter Piet Mondrian that year. Each wool jersey shift is pieced from separate blocks of color, and all of its shaping is hidden in the seams of the grid. The dresses brought wide attention to both designer and painter, and mass manufacturers soon copied them.

looks.name: Jumpsuit Dress
looks.description: This evening jumpsuit is cut in light chiffon, with wide palazzo-style legs. Evening jumpsuits of this kind belong to the late 1960s and 1970s, when long, fluid lines replaced the short A-line mini and trousers became a regular part of women's wardrobes. Emilio Pucci's silk jersey pyjama dress of about 1968, now in the V&A, is an early example.

looks.name: Blue Silk Dress
looks.description: This royal blue evening gown recalls one from the 1920s made of silk chiffon set with lace, with handkerchief panels over a crepe de chine lining. That gown belonged to Carrie Chapman Catt (1859-1947), who led the American women's suffrage movement to the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920, and she owned it during years of travel for suffrage and the League of Nations.

looks.name: Geoffrey Beene
looks.description: This evening gown and jacket by the American designer Geoffrey Beene date from the 1980s and come from the private collection of Iris Barrel Apfel. Beene founded his label in 1963. After the structured, architectural dresses of his early years, he turned to softly draped, loosely constructed clothes in lighter fabrics that suggested the body instead of gripping it.
